the `runblocking` here is safe because `datasource.factory.create()` is called by the [paging]( library inside `computablelivedata.compute()`, which runs on `archtaskexecutor.getiothreadexecutor()` (the default fetch executor). plus, the pre-room (wellsql) implementation was also synchronous/blocking on this same background thread — the `runblocking` wrapper was added to bridge the non-suspend `createdatasource` lambda with room's suspend dao queries, preserving the same threading behavior. fyi: and even if we wanted to refactor this further, to somehow remove `runblocking`, the only way to truly eliminate `runblocking` would be to not use `datasource.factory` at all — i.e., rewrite the paging layer to use [paging]( 's `pagingsource` which has a `suspend fun load()`. but that's a much larger refactor, well beyond the scope of this migration. ps: as such, the `runblocking` on the io executor is the correct approach here.
